body.text: The True Driver of Global Asset Valuations

Why does Central Bank Balance Sheets continue to command serious attention across finance? Beneath the surface narrative sits a practical framework that directly affects quality, speed, and long-term outcomes.

While retail investors obsess over central bank benchmark interest rates, institutional macro investors track an even more potent hydraulic force: the size and velocity of central bank balance sheets. When the Federal Reserve, ECB, or Bank of Japan conducts Quantitative Easing (QE) or Quantitative Tightening (QT), they directly expand or contract the world’s net fiat liquidity.
Accounting Mechanics of the Central Bank Balance Sheet

items: Assets: Domestic government debt securities (Treasuries) and mortgage-backed securities (MBS) purchased from primary dealers.
Liabilities: Currency in circulation, commercial bank reserves held at the central bank, and the Treasury General Account (TGA).
Overnight Reverse Repo Facility (ON RRP): A liquidity drain sponge absorbing excess cash from money market funds to maintain policy rate floors.
Passive QT Roll-Off: Allowing maturing government bonds to expire without reinvesting principal, draining corresponding commercial reserves.

body.text: Liquidity is the oxygen of financial markets. Central banks do not merely adjust borrowing costs. they expand and contract the total volume of air in the room.

body.text: The Ample Reserves Regime and Repo Spikes

If QT continues too long and bank reserves dip below the 'Lowest Comfortable Level of Reserves' (LCLoR), short-term overnight lending markets seize up, as occurred during the infamous September 2019 repo spike.
